title: A field localization upstairs identifies the base localization with its residue field
statement: Let $\varphi:R\to S$ be a flat homomorphism of commutative rings [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. Let $\mathfrak p\subset R$ be maximal and $\mathfrak q\subset S$ prime with $\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak q)=\mathfrak p$. Put $A=R_{\mathfrak p}$ and $B=S_{\mathfrak q}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. The canonical homomorphism $f:A\to B$, $r/s\mapsto\varphi(r)/\varphi(s)$, is well defined, flat, local (it maps $\mathfrak pA$ into $\mathfrak qB$), faithfully flat [def-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-ring-map], and injective. If $B$ is a field, then $\mathfrak pA=0$ and the canonical residue homomorphism $\rho:A\to R/\mathfrak p$, $r/s\mapsto\bar r/\bar s$, is an isomorphism of $R$-algebras. No Noetherian, finite type, or field-extension hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 00HT (lemma-flat-localization), parts (1),(2); Tag 00HR (lemma-local-flat-ff); Tag 05CK (lemma-faithfully-flat-universally-injective), zero-ideal case. Application to a field upstairs is the local-ring argument of Curves lemma-nodal, arbitrary-field descent paragraph.

proof.text: The equality $\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak q)=\mathfrak p$ ensures $\varphi(s)\notin\mathfrak q$ whenever $s\notin\mathfrak p$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-flat-local-ring-maps] to the given flat map and these primes: it gives exactly the well-defined map $f(r/s)=\varphi(r)/\varphi(s)$, its flatness, and locality $f(\mathfrak pA)\subseteq\mathfrak qB$. The local rings and their maximal ideals are those of [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime].

source.place: Tag 00HT, lemma-flat-localization, part (6); Tag 00HR, lemma-local-flat-ff; Tag 05CK, lemma-faithfully-flat-universally-injective.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-flat-local-hom-faithfully-flat] to this flat local map of local rings. Thus $f$ is faithfully flat. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-ideal-contraction] with the zero ideal of $A$: $f^{-1}(0)=0$, so $f$ is injective.

source.place: Tag 00HT, lemma-flat-localization, part (6); Tag 00HR, lemma-local-flat-ff; Tag 05CK, lemma-faithfully-flat-universally-injective.

proof.text: Now suppose $B$ is a field. Its proper maximal ideal $\mathfrak qB$ is zero: any nonzero element of an ideal in a field is a unit and would force the ideal to contain $1$. Locality gives $f(\mathfrak pA)=0$, and injectivity gives $\mathfrak pA=0$. Here [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] identifies $\mathfrak qB$ and $\mathfrak pA$ as the maximal ideals; no dimension or finiteness argument is used.

source.place: Elementary local-ring and fraction arguments completing the field case; compare literature/stacks-project/curves.tex, Tag 0C4D, lemma-nodal, arbitrary-field descent paragraph.

proof.text: For $s\notin\mathfrak p$, maximality gives $(s)+\mathfrak p=R$, so $us+v=1$ for some $u\in R$, $v\in\mathfrak p$; hence $\bar s$ is invertible in $R/\mathfrak p$. Define $\rho(r/s)=\bar r\bar s^{-1}$. If $r/s=r^{\prime}/s^{\prime}$, the fraction relation of [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] gives $t(rs^{\prime}-r^{\prime}s)=0$ with $t\notin\mathfrak p$; reduction and cancellation of $\bar t$ proves independence of representatives. The fraction addition and multiplication formulas prove that $\rho$ is a ring map and $\rho(r/1)=\bar r$, so it respects the $R$-actions. It is surjective since $\bar r=\rho(r/1)$. If $\rho(r/s)=0$, then $r\in\mathfrak p$, whence $r/1\in\mathfrak pA=0$ and $r/s=0$. Thus $\rho$ is bijective and its inverse is an $R$-algebra homomorphism, giving the asserted canonical isomorphism.
